questions.prompt: Match each tab of an item with what it holds.

pairs.right: The idea, the formula and a case worked by hand
A worked analysis of a dataset, with its results, figures and code
A new dataset to work, or questions to answer
The formulas, functions and sources, to look back at

questions.explanation: Learn teaches, Example shows the method on a dataset, Exercise checks that you can do it, and Reference is for looking things up later.

questions.prompt: In the list on the left, item 1.3 has the mark ◐. What does it mean?
options: You have started it, but it is not complete yet
It is locked until Module 0 is complete
questions.explanation: ✓ is complete, ◐ is started, ○ is not started. Nothing in the Course is locked: modules recommend what to do first, but you can open any item.

questions.prompt: You are on an Example and want to change one of its values to see what happens to the mean. What do you do?
options: Press Open in the Workbench, change the value there, and press Ctrl+L to come back
Type the new value into the Example's table
Sign out and sign in again
questions.explanation: The Course shows the Example as it was worked. Open in the Workbench copies it to the calculator, where every input can be changed. Course (Ctrl+L) takes you back to the item.

questions.prompt: You typed a mean of 52.3 in an Exercise and pressed Check my answers. It says "too high". What is the best next step?
options: Check the formula on the Learn tab and your arithmetic, or press Show a hint
Keep typing numbers a little lower until it is accepted
Open the Reference tab, which has the answer
Skip the item: it can never be completed after a wrong answer
questions.explanation: The message tells you which way you are off, so look for the mistake: the formula, a value left out, n − 1 instead of n. Guessing teaches nothing, and the module check will ask you to do it yourself. You can try an exercise as often as you like.

questions.prompt: You work on a lab computer that is wiped every weekend. Which of these keep your progress safe? Choose every one that applies.
options: Learner ▸ Back up my progress, to a USB drive or a cloud folder
Add learner from file, on the Who is learning? screen of the next computer
Using Just the Workbench instead of signing in
questions.explanation: A backup is a copy of your progress file; Add learner from file brings it back in on another computer, and combines it with any copy already there. The recovery code sets a new PIN if you forget yours. Just the Workbench records no progress at all.

questions.prompt: Which key shows help for the screen you are on? (Type the key, such as F5.)
questions.explanation: F1, or Help ▸ Help for this screen. In the Course it explains how the Course works; in the Workbench it opens the Instructions for the analysis you have chosen.
